title: Gordon Gray named in the MJ12 documents

tellings.quote: Gray was also named as one of the advisers on the top secret research and development organization established by Truman as it appears in the leaked Majestic [music] 12 documentation.

plain: Gordon Gray was one of the members of Majestic 12, a secret research group Truman set up in 1947, Michels says, citing the leaked MJ-12 documents. Those papers came to light in 1984 on a roll of film mailed with no name to a researcher named Jaime Shandera, and were made public in 1987. The FBI's copies are stamped "BOGUS," and the Air Force said they were "fabricated," while the physicist Stanton Friedman judged them "almost certainly genuine." The papers call the group "a TOP SECRET Research and Development/ Intelligence operation responsible directly and only to the President" and list "Mr. Gordon Gray" among its members; Michels' word "advisers" is his own, and Gray's part holds only as far as the papers are real.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper calls Majestic-12 "a TOP SECRET Research and Development/ Intelligence operation responsible directly and only to the President of the United States" and lists "Mr. Gordon Gray" among the members of the group Truman's order of 24 September 1947 established. Michels' "advisers" is his word for those members; the naming is the paper's, and Gray's part holds only as far as the paper is genuine.
